name: Beer pong
seoDesc: Beer pong: work out total beer expenses from the tables and the games to play. A free food calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: The Beer pong calculator turns the tables, the games to play, the cups per team per game and the tournament duration into total beer expenses. Think of it as a shortcut for portioning, timing or nutrition. The formula is printed further down, so you can check the answer by hand if you want to.

sections.title: How does the Beer pong calculator work?
sections.html:
The Beer pong calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports total beer expenses in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the sex); then you type in the tables, the games to play, the cups per team per game and the tournament duration.

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Beer pong calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Total beer expenses=expenses per person × teams × players per team
Beer per cup=(1 ÷ 2) × beer needed ÷ (cups per team per game × games to play)
Total beer expenses=beer needed × price of beer
Teams=games to play + 1
Beer per cup=beer per team per game ÷ cups per team per game
Blood alcohol content=the larger of (0, (1000 × raw alcohol, body weight, sex, tournament duration))

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
The form opens with a complete set of values: Players per team = 2, Tables = 1, Cups per team per game = 10 and Beer per team per game = 2 large bottles. Straight away the calculator returns Beer per cup = 0.2 large bottles.

Those are real numbers produced by the same engine that runs when you press Calculate, so you can change any single box afterwards and watch the answer move from this starting point.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: Beer per cup = 0.2 large bottles should be roughly the size you expected from Players per team = 2 and Tables = 1.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Beer pong calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Scaling a recipe up or down
  • Checking portions before you shop
  • Working out timing so everything finishes together
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the tables, the games to play and the cups per team per game — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Beer pong calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns total beer expenses, derived from the tables, the games to play and the cups per team per game. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Beer pong calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the tables, the games to play, the cups per team per game and the tournament duration, which is 10 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter beer per team per game in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Beer per team per game opens in 500 ml and the chip beside it offers 14 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There is one choice to make (1 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Beer per cup = 0.2 large bottles. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Beer pong calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
